title: Vivekachudamani
author: Sankaracharya (Madhavananda trans)
description: Vivekachudamani (The Crest-Jewel of Discrimination) of Sri Sankaracharya, with the Sanskrit text, English translation and notes by Swami Madhavananda of the Ramakrishna Order (Advaita Ashrama, Mayavati, first published 1921). Traditionally attributed to Adi Shankara (eighth century CE), the great exponent of Advaita Vedanta, this poem of some 580 verses is cast as a dialogue between a teacher and a disciple seeking freedom from the cycle of birth and death. It teaches the qualifications of the seeker, discrimination between the real and the unreal, the five sheaths (koshas) that veil the Self, the three bodies and three states of consciousness, the superimposition (adhyasa) of the not-self on the Self, and the realisation that Atman is identical with Brahman, the attainment of jivanmukti or liberation in life. Madhavananda's word-by-word translation makes it a standard study text of non-dual Vedanta.
